newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Little gain seen for Konka 97 net.
newsitem.headline: Little gain seen for Konka 97 net.

text.p: The expiry in 1997 of three years of preferential income tax status for Konka Group Co is expected to slow profit growth, company officials said on Friday.
The company currently enjoys 7.5 percent corporate tax, compared with the normal 15 percent, officials said, although they declined to say why it had been extended this privilege.

The television maker said in an annual report issued on Friday that its 1996 net profits climbed 29.1 percent to 346 million yuan, compared with 268 million posted in 1995 based on international accounting standards.
"Profits may dip in line with the 7.5 percentage point increase in income tax," a senior official told the Hong Kong-based newsletter China Securities Bulletin. He declined to elaborate.
Analysts said they saw no growth in Konka's 1997 profits.
"I think the 1997 net will stay at the 1996 level given the tax rate increase," an analyst at J&A Securities said.
Konka attributed the strong 1996 performance to increased production and sales, which boosted its share of the domestic colour television market to 13 percent from 1995's nine percent.
Turnover reached 5.01 billion yuan in 1996 compared with 3.48 billion the year earlier, the report said.
Konka's B shares ended Friday at HK$9.82, unchanged from Thursday. Volume was 94,100 shares.
Analaysts said they saw no impact on trade in the counter from the release of Friday's report.
Konka's board of directors proposed a cash dividend of 0.52 yuan per share based on 1996 profits, pending approval of shareholders at a meeting on May 12, the report said.
